messages.author: 17794b97fc9f11a0
messages.subject: Regarding sleep log
parts:
Hi all,

I have a quick question about basic usage. 

1. How does the output (especially sleep onset, wakeup time, etc.) differ when we are using a sleep log compared to when we are not using one?

2. The "guider_onset" and "guider_wakeup" columns in the "part4_nightsummary_sleep_cleaned.csv" file show readings like 25.128, 31.886, 32.097, etc. How should we interpret these readings?

3. One of my participants wore the watch for 7 consecutive days but had a non-wear period of more than 10 days afterward. The watch was recording during this time. How can I command GGIR to process the data only for the first 7 days?

Thank you.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Regarding sleep log
parts:
Hi anonymous,

  1. This should be clear from the vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#56_Sleep_analysis
  2. This should also be clear from the vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#42_Output_part_4
  3. See input arguments maxdur and max_calendar_dur: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIRParameters.html

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
